content:
maya: Heads up - we got a support ticket where a user’s fncall silently failed in canary. They see 200 but no tool invoked and no reject in console.
dan: do we have the raw request/response from canary logs? sounds like validation dropped the toolcall.
maya: pasted one in #incidents earlier but TL;DR: model returned a function-like object but shape mismatched (array vs object) and our code treated it as non-fatal, swallowed it.
leo: ugh. is that from strict-validate=on? I thought canary was running permissive soft-validate.
sasha: canary config is permissive but our coercion layer only logs at DEBUG and sample rate is 0.1. so most bad shapes never show up in SLO dashboards.
irene: the UX problem is users see no error and no retry. They assume model didn't call tool and keep resending prompts.
maya: proposal: make a short-term toggle to escalate coercion logs for canary traffic where fncall appears in model output but schema rejects. Add a line item in rollout checklist.
dan: agree. also we should surface a small counter in the console: "fncall-dropped-by-validator" with tags (route, model-version, canary).
leo: how expensive is bumping sample rate? metrics ingestion and retention cost will spike but for a 24h debug window should be fine.
sasha: ops-bot: note that we may need to increase logging retention if we want to backfill the last 48h. :warning: 
ops-bot: deploy scheduled: increased retention requires approval from finance. pinged @finance for a one-time lift.
irene: longer term: we need a soft-validate mode that returns a structured warning with the response, e.g. keep the toolcall in response but add "validation_warnings": [...]. That way callers can opt-in to degrade gracefully.
leo: can we implement that without big API changes? Maybe a header "X-Schema-Mode: warn" that the SDK can set.
dan: header sounds good for SDK clients, but platform should also allow route-level default. console toggle per-route would help teams who rely on strict semantics.
maya: also add telemetry: count of "toolcall-in-model-output" vs "toolcall-accepted" vs "toolcall-coerced". We need those three to reason about rates.
sasha: dashboard ask: a small panel in per-route metrics showing those counts + sample traces. I'll sketch a mock and drop it in the Roadmap doc.
leo: for immediate mitigation, I'll flip canary coercion logs to INFO and bump sample to 1.0 for 12h. will monitor cost.
irene: please also add an alert: if dropped-toolcall rate >0.5% for 10m then page oncall.
dan: should the alert page ops or eng-platform? page ops first then escalate to eng-platform.
maya: ok action list: (1) leo: bump sample & log level for 12h (2) sasha: dashboard mock + alert panel (3) dan: add console counter + route toggle design (4) irene: spec for X-Schema-Mode warn header and soft-validate payload shape.
leo: starting the log bump now. will post follow-up in this thread when done.
maya: thanks. if anyone sees customer ticket threads linking to this, pls add context and tag me.
leo: done - logs bumped, sample=1.0, retention increased for 48h. watching metrics.
sasha: mock uploaded: https://redwood.internal/designs/fncall-coercion-dashboard - feedback welcome.
irene: I'll draft the header design this afternoon. dan, can you add a short console UX wire for the per-route toggle?
dan: on it, will share a quick Figma frame in a few hours.
maya: great. closing the loop after we gather 12h of telemetry. thanks all :)
